105. In June 2022, 19% of women in prison, compared to 16% of men, were being held on
remand. In 2021, over half of women (52%) remanded and tried by the magistrates’ court
didn’t receive a custodial sentence. In the Crown Court, this figure was more than two in five
(43%).294

106. Women’s offending is commonly linked to underlying mental health needs, drug and alcohol
problems, coercive relationships, financial difficulties and debt:295
• Seventy six per cent of women in prison report having mental health issues (compared
with 51% of men).
• Forty six per cent of female prisoners have reported having attempted suicide at some
point in their life, compared with 21% of male prisoners and 6% in the general
population.296
• Fifty three per cent of female prisoners, compared to 27% of male prisoners, report
having experienced emotional, physical or sexual abuse as a child.
• It is estimated that nearly 60% of women who offend have experienced domestic
abuse.297
• Approximately 48% of women in prison have committed an offence in order to support
someone else’s drug habit298 – more than double the 22% of men who reported the
same.
• Twenty five per cent of women report having a drug or alcohol problem on entry to prison
(compared with 13% of men).299
• Thirty one per cent of female prisoners have spent time in local authority care.
